A vegan cheese that mainly consists of potato, oil and soy.

==Ingredients==

*5 ea. (750g–1kg) large, hard boiling potatoes
*20 ml [[cookbook:Soy Sauce|soy sauce]] or [[Cookbook:Yeast extract|yeast extract]]
*20 ml [[Cookbook:Margarine|margarine]] or [[Cookbook:Rapeseed Oil|rapeseed oil]]
*[[cookbook:Corn Flour|Corn flour]] or [[Cookbook:breading|breading]] mixture
*Any of the following optional ingredients:
**[[cookbook:salt|Salt]] or celery salt
**Bear's garlic or [[cookbook:garlic|garlic]]
**[[cookbook:herbs|Herbs]], e.g. [[Cookbook:paprika|paprika]], [[Cookbook:thyme|thyme]], [[Cookbook:rosemary|rosemary]], [[Cookbook:cumin|cumin]], [[Cookbook:oregano|oregano]] and [[Cookbook:savory|savory]]
**[[cookbook:onion|Onion]]s
**Taco seasoning mix (e.g. corn flour, salt, [[cookbook:Chili Pepper|chili]], onion, garlic, paprika, [[cookbook:MSG|sodium glutamate]])
**1–3 g chili seasoning mix (e.g. chilies, [[cookbook:Orange|orange]] [[Cookbook:zest|zest]], [[cookbook:Sesame Seed|sesame]], paprika, [[cookbook:celery|celery]], and [[cookbook:mustard|mustard]])
**1–5 g [[cookbook:Stock|vegetable stock]]
**[[cookbook:Sugar|Unrefined sugar]] (or sugar not refined using the char method)
**[[cookbook:pepper|Pepper]]
**10 ml [[cookbook:vinegar|vinegar]]

==Procedure==
#[[cookbook:Boil|Boil]] potatoes until they are not quite done. If the potatoes are not completely done the resulting substance may be sliceable, although it will be easy to spread anyway.
#[[Cookbook:Mashing|Mash]] the potatoes, then stir in the soy sauce.
#Mix in some margarine and cornflour. The substance should take on the consistency of [[cookbook:Peanut Butter|peanut butter]] but have more the color of cheese than anything else.
#Mix in any of the optional additions to add flavor to the mixture.
#Press the substance into a small, round form, to give it the form of a cheddar cheese. Unmold and serve.

== Notes, tips, and variations ==
[[Image:Bfast2005_vegan_cheese.jpg|Vegan cheese with rice|thumb]]

* A small amount of lecithin powder can be added as an emulgator but is not really necessary. Being hydrophilic and lipophilic, it binds together the water and the oil.
* Adding vinegar may increase durability in the refrigerator but more than 4 days are not recommended.
* A pinch of sugar can add to the taste but may not be compatible with all other spices.
* For a variant with rice, about half (and up to two-thirds) of the base substance is replaced by mashed rice. The advantage of mashed rice is that it results in a more cheese like substance, which dries better.
* A variant with vegetable stock can be made with less soy sauce. Mexican Taco Seasoning Mix can be used but is not required, because the vegetable stock is already very spicy. The variant can be combined with rice.
* A dairy free cheese flavor sauce mix can be suitable to acquire a stronger cheese flavor.
* Freezing is not recommended. There was a single case where freezing seemed to even have improved the consistency (making it a bit like tofu) but this lacks reproducibility.
* The cheese is best served slightly heated (e.g., on a solar oven) on [[Cookbook:Ciabatta|ciabatta]] with a splash of warm [[cookbook:Olive Oil|olive]] or rapeseed oil, mixed with a mashed clove of garlic and with a slice of [[cookbook:tomato|tomato]] and a leaf of [[Cookbook:Basil|basil]].
* Put the cheese on a slice of bread and sprinkle hackled onions on top. Bake in a toaster oven or [[cookbook:grilling|grill]] until the onions turn only slightly glassy. [[cookbook:Grape|Grapes]] cut in halves make a good topping and complement the taste.
